summary: The Netherlands is in the Schengen area, and EU nationals have the right to travel freely there. Under Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, nationals of the countries in its Annex II are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period, and nationals of the countries in Annex I must hold a visa; the Schengen Visa Code sets the visa fee at EUR 90. The EU says ETIAS, the travel authorisation that will be required of visa-exempt nationals, is currently not in operation.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any rolling 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area rather than per country. Leaving and coming back does not reset the allowance: the Schengen Borders Code counts the 180-day period preceding each day of stay, so days already spent anywhere in the area during that period still count against the 90. The day you enter counts as the first day of stay and the day you leave as the last.

source.instrument: Regulation (EU) 2016/399, Article 6(1) (90 days in any 180-day period, the 180 days preceding each day of stay) and Article 6(2) (the date of entry is the first day of stay and the date of exit the last)

fee.text: Applicants shall pay a visa fee of EUR 90.

processing.text: That period may be extended up to a maximum of 45 calendar days in individual cases, notably when further scrutiny of the application is needed.

stayDays.text: This Regulation establishes the procedures and conditions for issuing visas for intended stays on the territory of the Member States not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period.

extendable.text: The period of validity and/or the duration of stay of an issued visa shall be extended where the competent authority of a Member State considers that a visa holder has provided proof of force majeure or humanitarian reasons preventing him from leaving the territory of the Member States before the expiry of the period of validity of or the duration of stay authorised by the visa. Such an extension shall be granted free of charge. 2. The period of validity and/or the duration of stay of an issued visa may be extended if the visa holder provides proof of serious personal reasons justifying the extension of the period of validity or the duration of stay.

tips.text: The UK government says that if you are travelling to other Schengen countries as well, your whole visit must be within the 90-day limit, and that visits to Schengen countries within the previous 180 days count towards your 90 days.

Canada's travel advice says cyclists have priority over other traffic and that, on foot, you should make sure you are not inadvertently walking on a bike path, as these commonly run alongside sidewalks and are not always clearly marked. The UK FCDO says cycle paths are busy and cyclists ride at speed, and to look out for cyclists, mopeds and trams when crossing roads.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for the Netherlands?
faq.answer: No. The United States is in Annex II of Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period. The EU lists the United States among the countries whose nationals will need an ETIAS travel authorisation (EUR 20 application fee) once it starts; it is currently not in operation.

faq.question: How much does a Netherlands Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: Under the Schengen Visa Code the short-stay visa fee is EUR 90; children from six and below 12 pay EUR 45, and children under six are exempt.

faq.question: How do I stay in the Netherlands longer than 90 days?
faq.answer: The IND (Immigration and Naturalisation Service) handles applying for or extending a residence permit. Its fee table lists EUR 254 for a first application to stay with a family member (including a partner), for study, for researchers and for the orientation year, and EUR 423 for highly skilled migrants and for work in employment.

faq.question: What is the Dutch orientation year (zoekjaar) permit?
faq.answer: The IND lists it as a residence permit for looking for a job after study, promotion (doctorate) or scientific research, with a fee of EUR 254 for a first application. No official source we could read states the eligibility conditions.

faq.question: Is cash widely accepted in the Netherlands?
faq.answer: The Government of Canada says credit cards are not widely accepted in the Netherlands and advises making sure you have access to enough cash to cover your expenses during your trip.
